views.name: city_july_records_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  city_name AS city_name_original,
  insert_date AS date
FROM cities
WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
  AND substr(insert_date,1,7) = '2021-07'
views.description: Select all records for cities with country_code_2 = 'cn' and dates within July 2021. Do not collapse duplicates; keep one row per original record.

views.name: city_name_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cj.city_id AS city_id,
  cj.date AS date,
  -- Normalize: first letter uppercase, rest lowercase. Handle empty/null names.
  CASE
    WHEN cj.city_name_original IS NULL OR cj.city_name_original = '' THEN cj.city_name_original
    ELSE
      upper(substr(cj.city_name_original, 1, 1)) || lower(substr(cj.city_name_original, 2))
  END AS city_name
FROM city_july_records_sel AS cj
views.description: Normalize / canonicalize the city name to have first letter uppercase and the rest lowercase for each record.

views.name: distinct_date_per_city
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id AS city_id,
  c.insert_date AS date,
  c.city_name AS city_name
FROM cities c
JOIN (
  SELECT city_id, insert_date, MIN(rowid) AS keep_row
  FROM cities
  GROUP BY city_id, insert_date
) keepers ON keepers.city_id = c.city_id AND keepers.insert_date = c.insert_date AND keepers.keep_row = rowid
views.description: For each calendar date and city, pick exactly one record if multiple exist on the same date (any one). This yields one row per city+date.

views.name: city_date_streaks
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.city_id,
  d.date,
  d.city_name,
  MIN(d.date) OVER (PARTITION BY d.city_id, grp) AS streak_id,
  (JULIANDAY(MAX(d.date) OVER (PARTITION BY d.city_id, grp)) - JULIANDAY(MIN(d.date) OVER (PARTITION BY d.city_id, grp)) + 1) AS streak_length
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.city_id,
    r.date,
    r.city_name,
    (JULIANDAY(r.date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.city_id ORDER BY r.date)) AS grp
  FROM distinct_date_per_city AS r
) AS d
views.description: Identify contiguous streaks of consecutive calendar dates for each city by ordering dates and using date gap/lead/lag logic; assign a streak identifier and compute streak length and mark each date's streak start/end membership.

views.name: june_city_records
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  country_code_2 AS country_code,
  date(insert_date) AS record_date
FROM cities
WHERE date(insert_date) BETWEEN date('2022-06-02') AND date('2022-06-02')

semantic_filters.insert_date: rows whose insert_date falls in June 2022 (restricted to available DB date values)

views.description: Select all records whose inserted city date falls in June 2022 (i.e., dates between 2022-06-01 and 2022-06-30 inclusive). Keep the country code and the date (as a date without time).

views.name: country_day_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code AS country_code,
  record_date AS record_date,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_record_flag
FROM june_city_records
GROUP BY country_code, record_date
views.description: For each country and calendar day in June 2022, produce one row per country/day indicating whether that country has at least one record on that day (deduplicate multiple records per day).

views.name: jan2022_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id AS row_id,
  country_code_2 AS country,
  city_name AS city,
  insert_date AS insertion_date
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date >= '2022-01-01' AND insert_date <= '2022-01-31'
views.description: All rows restricted to insertion dates within January 1–31, 2022 (inclusive), keeping country, city, insertion_date and any row identifier needed for counting rows.

views.name: country_daily_presence
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cc.country_name AS country,
  c.insert_date AS date,
  COUNT(*) AS rows_on_date,
  cc.country_id,
  c.city_id
FROM cities c
JOIN cities_countries cc
  ON c.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
WHERE c.insert_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'
GROUP BY cc.country_name, c.insert_date, cc.country_id

semantic_filters.date_range: January 2022 (inclusive) - intrinsic filter applied via insert_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'

views.description: For each country and calendar date in January 2022 that has one or more rows, produce one row per country-date indicating presence and the count of rows on that date.

views.name: country_consecutive_spans
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cdp.country AS country,
  DATE(MIN(cdp.date)) AS span_start,
  DATE(MAX(cdp.date)) AS span_end,
  CAST((JULIANDAY(MAX(cdp.date)) - JULIANDAY(MIN(cdp.date)) + 1) AS INTEGER) AS span_length_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    country,
    date,
    DATE(date, '-' || seq || ' day') AS date_minus_seq
  FROM (
    SELECT
      country,
      date,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY date) - 1 AS seq
    FROM (
      SELECT DISTINCT country, date
      FROM country_daily_presence
      WHERE strftime('%Y', date) = '2022' AND strftime('%m', date) = '01'
    )
  )
) AS cdp
GROUP BY cdp.country, cdp.date_minus_seq
views.description: For each country, compute consecutive-day spans (contiguous calendar dates within Jan 2022) where the country has presence on every day; produce one row per span with span_start, span_end and span_length_days.

views.name: country_nine_date_candidates_with_span_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cc.country_name AS country,
  spans.span_start AS longest_span_start,
  spans.span_end AS longest_span_end,
  spans.span_length_days AS longest_span_length_days,
  -- count total entries in cities table for this country within the span (by country_code_2 matching country_code_2 from cities_countries)
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cities c
     WHERE c.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
       AND date(c.insert_date) >= date(spans.span_start)
       AND date(c.insert_date) <= date(spans.span_end)
  ) AS total_entries_in_longest_period,
  -- count entries from the capital city: join cities to countries to find capital city (capital=1) for that country_code_2, compare city_name
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cities c
     WHERE c.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
       AND date(c.insert_date) >= date(spans.span_start)
       AND date(c.insert_date) <= date(spans.span_end)
       AND c.city_name = (
         SELECT city_name FROM cities cap
          WHERE cap.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2 AND cap.capital = 1
          LIMIT 1
       )
  ) AS entries_from_capital_in_longest_period
FROM cities_countries cc
JOIN (
  -- choose spans that are maximal length for each country based on country_consecutive_spans concept derived from cities_countries + cities insert_date
  SELECT
    t.country_name,
    t.country_code_2,
    s.span_start,
    s.span_end,
    s.span_length_days
  FROM (
    -- compute consecutive-day spans per country using distinct dates from cities.insert_date
    SELECT
      cc_inner.country_name,
      cc_inner.country_code_2,
      date(d.date) AS span_start,
      date(d.date) AS span_end,
      1 AS span_length_days
    FROM cities_countries cc_inner
    JOIN (
      SELECT DISTINCT country_code_2, date(insert_date) AS date FROM cities
    ) d ON d.country_code_2 = cc_inner.country_code_2

    UNION ALL

    -- To build multi-day spans we self-join adjacent dates iteratively by computing runs using gap-and-island technique:
    SELECT
      country_name,
      country_code_2,
      MIN(date) AS span_start,
      MAX(date) AS span_end,
      CAST((julianday(MAX(date)) - julianday(MIN(date)) + 1) AS INTEGER) AS span_length_days
    FROM (
      SELECT
        cc_inner2.country_name,
        cc_inner2.country_code_2,
        date(d2.date) AS date,
        date(d2.date, '-' || (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cc_inner2.country_code_2 ORDER BY date(d2.date)) - 1) || ' days') AS island_key
      FROM cities_countries cc_inner2
      JOIN (
        SELECT DISTINCT country_code_2, date(insert_date) AS date FROM cities
      ) d2 ON d2.country_code_2 = cc_inner2.country_code_2
    )
    GROUP BY country_name, country_code_2, island_key
  ) s
  JOIN cities_countries t ON t.country_code_2 = s.country_code_2 AND t.country_name = s.country_name
) spans ON spans.country_name = cc.country_name AND spans.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
-- filter countries that have presence on exactly nine distinct January 2022 dates:
WHERE (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT date(c2.insert_date))
  FROM cities c2
  WHERE c2.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
    AND strftime('%Y-%m', c2.insert_date) = '2022-01'
) = 9
-- ensure span is one of the longest for the country
AND spans.span_length_days = (
  SELECT MAX(s2.span_length_days)
  FROM (
    SELECT
      CAST((julianday(MAX(date)) - julianday(MIN(date)) + 1) AS INTEGER) AS span_length_days,
      country_code_2
    FROM (
      SELECT
        country_code_2,
        date(date) AS date,
        date(date, '-' || (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code_2 ORDER BY date(date)) - 1) || ' days') AS island_key
      FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT country_code_2, date(insert_date) AS date FROM cities
      )
    )
    GROUP BY country_code_2, island_key
  ) s2
  WHERE s2.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
)
views.description: Identify countries that have presence on exactly nine distinct January 2022 dates, join to that country's longest consecutive span (choose the span(s) with maximal length; if multiple equal-length spans exist for the country they should all be available), and for each such span compute counts of rows within that span and counts where city equals the country's capital (city equality decided by later schema alignment).

views.name: city_inserts_filtered_months_years
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CASE CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN 1 THEN 'January'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'February'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'March'
    WHEN 4 THEN 'April'
    WHEN 5 THEN 'May'
    WHEN 6 THEN 'June'
    WHEN 7 THEN 'July'
    WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
    WHEN 9 THEN 'September'
    WHEN 10 THEN 'October'
    WHEN 11 THEN 'November'
    WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
  END AS month_name
FROM cities
WHERE year IN (2021, 2022, 2023)
  AND month_name IN ('April', 'May', 'June')
views.description: Select individual city insert events restricted to the months April, May, and June and years 2021–2023. Keep the event's calendar year and month name so later steps can aggregate by month and year.

views.name: monthly_city_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  strftime('%m', insert_date) AS month_num,
  CASE strftime('%m', insert_date)
    WHEN '01' THEN 'January' WHEN '02' THEN 'February' WHEN '03' THEN 'March'
    WHEN '04' THEN 'April' WHEN '05' THEN 'May' WHEN '06' THEN 'June'
    WHEN '07' THEN 'July' WHEN '08' THEN 'August' WHEN '09' THEN 'September'
    WHEN '10' THEN 'October' WHEN '11' THEN 'November' WHEN '12' THEN 'December'
  END AS month_name,
  COUNT(*) AS monthly_total
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY year, month_num, month_name
views.description: Aggregate the filtered city insert events to compute the count of newly inserted cities per year and month (monthly_total). One row per year+month.

views.name: running_totals_by_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mc.year AS year,
  mc.month_name AS month_name,
  mc.monthly_total AS monthly_total,
  (
    SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
    FROM monthly_city_counts m2
    WHERE m2.year >= 2021
      AND (m2.year < mc.year
           OR (m2.year = mc.year AND
               (CASE m2.month_name
                    WHEN 'January' THEN 1 WHEN 'February' THEN 2 WHEN 'March' THEN 3
                    WHEN 'April' THEN 4 WHEN 'May' THEN 5 WHEN 'June' THEN 6
                    WHEN 'July' THEN 7 WHEN 'August' THEN 8 WHEN 'September' THEN 9
                    WHEN 'October' THEN 10 WHEN 'November' THEN 11 WHEN 'December' THEN 12
                    ELSE NULL END)
               <=
               (CASE mc.month_name
                    WHEN 'January' THEN 1 WHEN 'February' THEN 2 WHEN 'March' THEN 3
                    WHEN 'April' THEN 4 WHEN 'May' THEN 5 WHEN 'June' THEN 6
                    WHEN 'July' THEN 7 WHEN 'August' THEN 8 WHEN 'September' THEN 9
                    WHEN 'October' THEN 10 WHEN 'November' THEN 11 WHEN 'December' THEN 12
                    ELSE NULL END)
          )
      )
  ) AS running_total
FROM monthly_city_counts mc
WHERE mc.year >= 2021
  AND mc.month_name IN ('April','May','June')
views.description: For each month (April/May/June) compute a cumulative running total of monthly_total ordered by year ascending, starting with 2021. Produces running_total for each year+month row.

views.name: yoy_growth_and_final_filter
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  r.month_name AS month_name,
  r.monthly_total AS monthly_total,
  r.running_total AS running_total,
  CASE
    WHEN p.monthly_total IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.monthly_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((r.monthly_total - p.monthly_total) * 1.0) / p.monthly_total
  END AS monthly_yoy_growth_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN p.running_total IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.running_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((r.running_total - p.running_total) * 1.0) / p.running_total
  END AS running_yoy_growth_pct
FROM running_totals_by_month r
LEFT JOIN running_totals_by_month p
  ON p.month_name = r.month_name
  AND p.year = r.year - 1
WHERE r.year NOT IN (2021)
views.description: Join each year+month row to the prior year's same-month row to compute year-over-year percentage growth for monthly_total and running_total (NULL if prior year's value is zero). Then filter out year 2021 so final output contains only years 2022 and 2023 and order will be applied externally.

views.name: postings_base_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_id AS posting_id,
  job_title_short AS job_title,
  salary_year_avg AS annual_average_salary,
  CASE
    WHEN job_work_from_home = 1 THEN 1
    WHEN job_location = 'Remote, OR' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS remote_flag,
  job_location AS location
FROM job_postings_fact
WHERE job_title_short = 'Data Analyst'
  AND salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select job postings that satisfy the basic filters: job title exactly 'Data Analyst', annual average salary is not null, and the posting indicates remote work (e.g., explicit remote flag true or location equals 'Remote'). Keep one row per posting and retain identifiers needed to join to skills and salary fields.

views.name: posting_skills
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sj.job_id AS posting_id,
  s.skills AS skill
FROM skills_job_dim sj
JOIN skills_dim s
  ON sj.skill_id = s.skill_id
WHERE sj.job_id IS NOT NULL
  AND s.skills IS NOT NULL
views.description: List each skill mentioned on a posting as one row (explode / unnest skill lists). This produces one row per posting-skill pair for postings of interest (no filtering to top-k here).

views.name: skill_frequencies
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.skills AS skill,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sj.job_id) AS posting_count
FROM skills_dim s
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim sj
  ON s.skill_id = sj.skill_id
LEFT JOIN job_postings_fact j
  ON sj.job_id = j.job_id
GROUP BY s.skills
views.description: Compute the frequency (count of distinct postings) for each skill among the base cohort of postings; one row per skill with its posting count.

views.name: final_included_postings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.posting_id AS posting_id,
  p.annual_average_salary AS annual_average_salary,
  s.skill AS matched_skill
FROM
  postings_base_cohort p
JOIN
  posting_skills s
  ON p.posting_id = s.posting_id
JOIN
  skill_frequencies f
  ON s.skill = f.skill
WHERE
  f.skill IN (
    SELECT skill FROM skill_frequencies
    ORDER BY posting_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
  )
views.description: Identify postings from the base cohort that list at least one skill belonging to the top-three most frequent skills (the top-k selection is applied when joining skill_frequencies). Produce one row per included posting with its salary and the matched skill(s) for potential reporting.

views.name: cohort_first_terms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  MIN(lt.term_start) AS first_term_start_date,
  CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', MIN(lt.term_start)) AS INTEGER) AS start_year
FROM legislators l
JOIN legislators_terms lt ON lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
GROUP BY l.id_bioguide
HAVING first_term_start_date >= '1917-01-01' AND first_term_start_date <= '1999-12-31'
views.description: Select the cohort of legislators whose first-ever term start date falls within an inclusive date range (1917-01-01 to 1999-12-31). One row per legislator with their canonical first_term_start_date and any identifier needed to link to term records.

views.name: all_terms_by_legislator
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(lt.term_start) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE date(lt.term_start)
  END AS term_start_date,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(lt.term_end) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE date(lt.term_end)
  END AS term_end_date
FROM legislators_terms lt
WHERE lt.id_bioguide IS NOT NULL
views.description: All recorded terms/office-holdings for legislators (one row per term) with start_date and end_date normalized; end_date may be NULL for ongoing terms. This relation will be used to determine whether a legislator was in office on a particular date.
validated_on: Based on the state each female legislator first represented, which state has the highest number of female legislators whose terms included December 31st at any point, and what is that count? Please provide the state's abbreviation.

views.name: cohort_dec31_statuses
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cft.legislator_id AS legislator_id,
  yrs.year_number AS year_number,
  date(printf('%04d-12-31', cft.start_year + yrs.year_number)) AS check_date,
  CASE
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM all_terms_by_legislator at
      WHERE at.legislator_id = cft.legislator_id
        AND date(at.term_start_date) <= date(printf('%04d-12-31', cft.start_year + yrs.year_number))
        AND date(at.term_end_date)   >= date(printf('%04d-12-31', cft.start_year + yrs.year_number))
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_office_flag
FROM
  cohort_first_terms cft,
  (SELECT 1 AS year_number UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
   UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
   UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15
   UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20
  ) yrs
views.description: For each cohort legislator and for each year_number 1..20, produce the calendar date to check (December 31 of start_year + year_number) and join to that legislator's term rows to determine if any term covers that date. This produces one row per legislator per year_number with a boolean flag indicating presence in office on that date.

views.name: retention_rates_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cd.year_number AS year_number,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cd.legislator_id) AS cohort_size,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.in_office_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retained_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT cd.legislator_id) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN cd.in_office_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT cd.legislator_id)
  END AS retention_rate
FROM cohort_dec31_statuses cd
GROUP BY cd.year_number
views.description: Aggregate the per-legislator-per-year presence flags to compute, for each year_number (1..20), the cohort_size (count of distinct cohort legislators), retained_count (count of legislators with in_office_flag true), and retention_rate = retained_count / cohort_size.

views.name: legislator_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  l.gender AS sex,
  t.state AS state,
  MIN(t.term_start) AS first_term_date
FROM legislators l
JOIN legislators_terms t
  ON l.id_bioguide = t.id_bioguide
WHERE l.gender = 'M'
  AND t.state = 'LA'
GROUP BY l.id_bioguide, l.gender, t.state
views.description: Select the cohort of legislators filtered to male legislators from the state of Louisiana, with their identifiers and their recorded first_term_date (the date their first term began). One row per legislator in the filtered cohort.

views.name: service_status_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  term_start AS service_start_date,
  term_end AS service_end_date
FROM legislators_terms
WHERE term_start IS NOT NULL OR term_end IS NOT NULL
views.description: All service (tenure) records or status events for legislators that record when a legislator was serving (start and end dates for service segments). One row per service segment/event for a legislator.

views.name: target_dates_per_legislator_years
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.legislator_id AS legislator_id,
  yrs.years_since_first_term AS years_since_first_term,
  printf('%04d-12-31', CAST(strftime('%Y', c.first_term_start_date) AS INTEGER) + yrs.years_since_first_term) AS target_date
FROM
  cohort_first_terms c,
  (SELECT 31 AS years_since_first_term UNION ALL
   SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL
   SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL
   SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL
   SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL
   SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49) yrs
views.description: For each legislator from the filtered cohort, produce one row per integer years_since_first_term value of interest (31..49), computing the target_date which is December 31 of (year(first_term_date) + years_since_first_term). This produces candidate target dates to check active service against for each legislator.

views.name: legislator_active_on_target
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.legislator_id AS legislator_id,
  t.years_since_first_term AS years_since_first_term,
  t.target_date AS target_date,
  CASE WHEN s.service_start_date <= t.target_date AND t.target_date <= s.service_end_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_active_on_target
FROM target_dates_per_legislator_years AS t
JOIN service_status_events AS s
  ON t.legislator_id = s.legislator_id
WHERE (s.service_start_date IS NOT NULL AND s.service_end_date IS NOT NULL)
  AND (t.target_date IS NOT NULL)
views.description: Join candidate target dates to service segments to determine, for each legislator and years_since_first_term row, whether the legislator was actively serving on that target_date (i.e., target_date falls within any service_start_date..service_end_date). Output one row per legislator and years_since_first_term for which the legislator is active on the target date.

views.name: female_legislator_terms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  lt.term_start AS term_start_date,
  lt.term_end AS term_end_date,
  lt.state AS state_abbreviation
FROM legislators_terms lt
JOIN legislators l
  ON lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
WHERE l.gender = 'F'
views.description: All term records for legislators who are female, keeping their identifiers and term date ranges and associated state for each term.

views.name: legislator_first_state
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  state AS first_state_abbreviation,
  MIN(term_start) AS first_term_start_date
FROM legislators_terms
GROUP BY id_bioguide
views.description: For each legislator, determine the state abbreviation from the term with the earliest term_start_date (their first-represented state).

views.name: first_state_female_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lfs.first_state_abbreviation AS state_abbreviation,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lfs.legislator_id) FILTER (WHERE ll.gender = 'F') AS female_legislator_count
FROM
  legislator_first_state lfs
JOIN
  legislators ll
  ON ll.id_bioguide = lfs.legislator_id
GROUP BY
  lfs.first_state_abbreviation
views.description: For each legislator who has any term including a December 31 (from terms_including_dec31), associate their first-represented state (from legislator_first_state) and produce one row per first-state with the distinct count of such female legislators.

views.name: legislator_terms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide AS legislator_id,
  lt.state AS state_abbreviation,
  l.gender AS gender,
  -- normalize term dates by casting to TEXT (they are stored as TEXT) and ensuring NULLs are preserved
  lt.term_start AS term_start_date,
  lt.term_end AS term_end_date,
  -- canonical first term start per legislator: derive by taking the minimum term_start from legislators_terms per id_bioguide
  (SELECT MIN(term_start) FROM legislators_terms WHERE id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide) AS first_term_start_date
FROM legislators_terms lt
JOIN legislators l ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
WHERE lt.state IS NOT NULL
  AND lt.term_start IS NOT NULL
  AND lt.term_end IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.state_abbreviation: US states only (filtered by non-null state)

views.description: All legislators' term records with start and end dates, gender, state, and a canonical first_term_start date per legislator. This filters to US states and ensures date fields are normalized but does not compute retention yet.

views.name: retention_checks_by_offset
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.legislator_id AS legislator_id,
  lt.state AS state_abbreviation,
  l.gender AS gender,
  offsets.offset_years AS offset_years,
  DATE(substr(lt.term_start,1,4) || '-' || '12-31') + (offsets.offset_years || ' years') AS check_date,
  CASE
    WHEN DATE(DATE(substr(lt.term_start,1,4) || '-' || '12-31') + (offsets.offset_years || ' years')) BETWEEN DATE(at.term_start_date) AND DATE(at.term_end_date) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_serving_on_check_date
FROM
  (SELECT id_bioguide AS legislator_id, MIN(term_start) AS first_term_start
   FROM legislators_terms
   WHERE term_start IS NOT NULL
   GROUP BY id_bioguide) t
JOIN legislators l ON l.id_bioguide = t.legislator_id
JOIN legislators_terms lt ON lt.id_bioguide = t.legislator_id AND lt.term_start = t.first_term_start
CROSS JOIN (SELECT 0 AS offset_years UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 10) offsets
LEFT JOIN (SELECT id_bioguide AS legislator_id, term_start AS term_start_date, COALESCE(term_end, '9999-12-31') AS term_end_date FROM legislators_terms) at
  ON at.legislator_id = t.legislator_id
views.description: For each legislator and for each evaluated offset year (0,2,4,6,8,10), produce a row indicating the target check date (December 31 of first_term_start_year + offset) and whether the legislator is serving on that date (boolean). Only include offsets within 0..10.

views.name: retention_rates_by_state_gender_offset
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.state_abbreviation AS state_abbreviation,
  r.gender AS gender,
  r.offset_years AS offset_years,
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.is_serving_on_check_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retained_count,
  COUNT(r.legislator_id) AS eligible_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(r.legislator_id) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN r.is_serving_on_check_date THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(r.legislator_id)
  END AS retention_rate
FROM retention_checks_by_offset r
GROUP BY
  r.state_abbreviation,
  r.gender,
  r.offset_years
views.description: For each state, gender, and offset year, compute retention rate as the fraction of legislators from that state+gender whose is_serving_on_check_date is true for that offset. Keep counts and denominators for later >0 checks.

views.name: states_with_nonzero_retention_both_genders_all_offsets
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.state_abbreviation AS state_abbreviation,
  CASE
    WHEN MIN(CASE WHEN r.gender = 'M' THEN (r.retention_rate > 0) ELSE 1 END) = 1
     AND MIN(CASE WHEN r.gender = 'F' THEN (r.retention_rate > 0) ELSE 1 END) = 1
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS meets_both_genders_nonzero_at_all_offsets,
  -- preserve keys to keep joinable: include state + gender + offset with aggregates folded per state
  NULL AS preservation_state_key_placeholder
FROM retention_rates_by_state_gender_offset r
WHERE r.offset_years IN (0,2,4,6,8,10)
GROUP BY r.state_abbreviation
views.description: For each state, determine whether for every offset in {0,2,4,6,8,10} both male and female retention_rate > 0; produce one row per state for states that satisfy this condition.

views.name: aliens_by_state
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(a.id, ad.id) AS alien_id,
  COALESCE(al.current_location, ad.current_location) AS state,
  -- age available only in alien_data
  ad.age AS age,
  -- determine friendly vs hostile from aggressive flag: aggressive = 0 -> friendly, 1 -> hostile
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ad.aggressive, ad.aggressive) = 0 THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_friendly,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ad.aggressive, ad.aggressive) = 1 THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_hostile
FROM aliens a
LEFT JOIN aliens_details adt ON a.id = adt.detail_id
LEFT JOIN aliens_location al ON a.id = al.loc_id
LEFT JOIN alien_data ad ON a.id = ad.id
views.description: All alien records with their state, age, and disposition flags (e.g., friendly vs hostile). This selects the base cohort of aliens and necessary attributes for aggregation.

views.name: state_population_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(a.state, l.state) AS state,
  COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(a.id, l.loc_id)) AS total_population,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(a.aggressive, 0) = 0 AND COALESCE(a.id, -1) != -1 THEN 1
           WHEN COALESCE(a.aggressive, 0) = 0 AND COALESCE(a.id, -1) = -1 AND COALESCE(l.loc_id, -1) != -1 AND 0=0 THEN 1
           ELSE 0 END) AS friendly_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(a.aggressive, 0) = 1 AND COALESCE(a.id, -1) != -1 THEN 1
           WHEN COALESCE(a.aggressive, 0) = 1 AND COALESCE(a.id, -1) = -1 AND COALESCE(l.loc_id, -1) != -1 AND 1=1 THEN 1
           ELSE 0 END) AS hostile_count,
  SUM(a.age) AS sum_age,
  COUNT(a.age) AS count_age
FROM alien_data a
FULL OUTER JOIN aliens_location l ON a.current_location = l.current_location AND a.state = l.state
GROUP BY COALESCE(a.state, l.state)
views.description: Aggregate counts and basic sums per state: total alien population, count of friendly aliens, count of hostile aliens, and sum (or average) of ages needed to compute average age.

views.name: state_percentages_and_avg_age
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  spc.state AS state,
  spc.total_population AS total_population,
  CASE WHEN spc.total_population = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE (CAST(spc.friendly_count AS REAL) / spc.total_population) * 100.0
  END AS friendly_percentage,
  CASE WHEN spc.total_population = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE (CAST(spc.hostile_count AS REAL) / spc.total_population) * 100.0
  END AS hostile_percentage,
  CASE WHEN spc.total_population = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE CAST(spc.sum_age AS REAL) / NULLIF(spc.count_age, 0)
  END AS average_age
FROM state_population_counts spc
views.description: Compute derived metrics per state: friendly percentage, hostile percentage, and average alien age, derived from the aggregated counts/sums.

views.name: top_states_with_filters
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.state AS state,
  sp.total_population AS total_population,
  sp.friendly_percentage AS friendly_percentage,
  sp.hostile_percentage AS hostile_percentage,
  sp.average_age AS average_age
FROM state_percentages_and_avg_age sp
WHERE sp.friendly_percentage > sp.hostile_percentage
  AND sp.average_age > 200

semantic_filters.top_n_placeholder: N (to be set to 10 in final query)

views.description: Order states by total alien population descending, take the top-N (the final query will use N=10), and keep only those rows where friendly_percentage > hostile_percentage and average_age > 200.
